data.name: One Troll Army
data.detailed_description:
Crush hundreds of minions as the powerful giant troll!
Tiny Goblins call on you to protect their fort, in exchange for armor, money and new moves to smash and loot minions!
Goblins build towers, barracks and catapults over each wave to help you fight back bigger minions and bosses!

Play Against The Twitch Chat! Enable Twitch integration to allow your viewers to directly control units


  • Fight as a boss troll with 12 upgradeable skills. Kick, Knock, Wheel, Quake, Taunt, Jump, Ram and Loot your way through the horde!
  • Defeat various enemies: from small rats to huge ballista-wielding rhino and buffalo bosses. 21 types of enemies and 15 bosses.
  • Manage the crowd of goblins. Make them builders, looters, miners, loggers and more to harvest resources, restore the fort, get the loot and build new structures.
  • Manage the fort. Build and upgrade 7 buildings with 3 levels of upgrades from small huts to great castles.
  • Build and upgrade defense towers. Each fort has 4 towers with 4 types of weapons (stone-thrower, archer, catapult, bomber). Also upgrade weapon types at the barracks.
  • Hire and upgrade orc mercenaries for support- but don’t let them die on the battlefield!
  • More than 50 goals and achievements.

reviews.review:
One Troll Army is a fun little tower defense game that gives me a much more active role than I usually get in this type of game. I am playing as a giant troll protecting a goblin fort while waves of enemies keep coming towards me. Instead of sitting back and letting my towers do everything, I can jump into the fight myself and smash enemies with different troll abilities. I like that idea because it makes the game feel like a mix of tower defense and simple action combat rather than just another game where I place towers and watch them work.

The troll itself is probably the best part for me. I can upgrade 12 different skills and use attacks such as kicking, ramming, jumping, knocking enemies around and causing earthquakes. I can run around the battlefield and deal with enemies that are getting too close to the fort, while the goblins and defensive structures handle other parts of the attack. I enjoy having to decide when I should fight personally and when I should focus more on the fort. It gives me something to do during every wave instead of making the combat feel completely automatic.

There is also a decent amount of building and resource management underneath the action. The goblins can take different jobs such as building, mining, logging and collecting loot, while I can improve seven different buildings across three upgrade levels. I can also build defensive towers with different weapons and upgrade those through the barracks. Orc mercenaries can be hired to help me in battle too. I like how all these systems connect because protecting the fort is not just about killing whatever happens to be closest to me. I have to keep the economy and defenses moving as the attacks get stronger.

The enemy variety is another strong point. There are 21 types of enemies and 15 bosses, so the waves are not completely identical from start to finish. The bosses can also put more pressure on my defenses because I cannot always deal with them in the same way as the smaller enemies. I like the general progression because the fort starts off looking pretty basic and gradually becomes a much stronger defensive position. Watching the buildings and defenses improve gives me a good feeling of actually building something rather than simply surviving one wave after another.

The biggest problem for me is that the core loop can become repetitive. I am still protecting the same basic type of fort, collecting resources, upgrading buildings and smashing waves of enemies, so after I have spent enough time with it the novelty starts to disappear. The controls and combat are simple too, which is good for getting started but means there is not a huge amount to master. I also think the strategy is more about managing everything efficiently than making complicated tactical decisions. That works for a casual tower defense game, but it limits how deep I can get into it.

I also think the Twitch integration is a clever idea, although it is more of an extra feature than something I need for the main experience. The game can allow a Twitch chat to control units while I play as the boss troll, which fits the chaotic nature of the game really well. I like that the developers experimented with something different instead of making a completely standard tower defense game. The presentation is simple and a little dated now, but the colourful fantasy style suits the ridiculous idea of a giant troll defending a castle with a crowd of goblins.

Overall, One Troll Army is a surprisingly enjoyable free tower defense game that works because it lets me take part in the fighting instead of only managing defenses from a distance. I like the troll abilities, fort upgrades, goblin jobs, towers, mercenaries and variety of enemies, and there is enough progression to keep me interested for a while. The main weakness is that the gameplay eventually becomes repetitive and the strategy is not as deep as the best tower defense games. Still, the combination of active troll combat and base management gives it enough personality to stand out, and I think it is worth playing when I want something simple that I can jump into without much commitment.

Rating: 7.3/10
